# semrel — Semantic Release Automation Without Node.js

**The zero-dependency, Go-native open-source alternative to `semantic-release`, `GoReleaser`, `release-please`, `release-it`, and `changesets`.**

---

**semrel** is an open-source, zero-dependency **semantic release** and **Semantic Versioning (SemVer)** automation engine written in Go. Shipped as a single static binary (~12 MB) with **zero Node.js runtime overhead**, `semrel` parses [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), computes the next SemVer version (`major`, `minor`, `patch`, or prerelease), generates Keep-a-Changelog Markdown/HTML release notes, updates manifests across **15+ language ecosystems**, builds Linux packages (`.deb`, `.rpm`, `.apk`), publishes to package and container registries, and creates releases on GitHub (including GHES), GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo, and Bitbucket — in **~1.4 seconds**.

> **Status:** Core pipeline, 46 official plugins, lockfile verification, and CI/CD integrations are production-proven and self-versioned via `semrel`. See [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) for the path to v1.0.0 and [Go version monitoring](docs/GO-VERSION-MONITORING.md) for weekly toolchain updates.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| **Auto SemVer from Commits** | **✅ Conventional Commits & Regex** | ✅ Conventional Commits | ❌ Manual Git tags (OSS) | ✅ Release PRs | ✅ / ❌ Manual changesets |
| **Scope-Based Bump Rules** | **✅ Built-in** | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Air-Gap / Offline CI** | **✅ Native (`.semrel.lock` + SHA-256)** | ❌ Requires npm registry | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Supply-Chain Security** | **✅ Cosign v3 + SBOM + SLSA L1** | ❌ 400+ transitive npm deps | ✅ Cosign + SBOM | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Plugin Ecosystem** | **46 official plugins (any binary)** | JavaScript-only npm packages | Built-in Go steps | Hardcoded | JavaScript-only |
| **Monorepo Workspaces** | **✅ 100% Free (`semrel workspace`)** | ✅ Community plugins | 💰 Pro tier ($3,300/yr) | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Enterprise / GHES / Free** | **✅ Apache 2.0 ($0 forever)** | ✅ MIT | 💰 Pro paywall | ✅ Apache 2.0 | ✅ MIT |

## Key Features

- 🔍 **Conventional Commits & Scope Rules** — Configurable SemVer bump rules by commit type, scope, breaking changes, and custom regex patterns.
- ⚡ **Zero Node.js Tax** — Single static Go binary (~12 MB). No `actions/setup-node`, no `npm install`, no 60-second cold starts, and zero npm supply-chain exposure.
- 🔌 **46 Official Standalone Plugins** — Modular 8-category pipeline (`condition`, `analyzer`, `generator`, `updater`, `packager`, `publisher`, `provider`, `hook`).
- 🔒 **Reproducible & Air-Gap Safe (`.semrel.lock`)** — Pin every plugin binary by SHA-256 checksum and restore offline via `semrel plugin restore` for NIS2/DORA-compliant pipelines.
- 🏗️ **Monorepo Workspace Engine (`semrel workspace`)** — Independent or lockstep versioning, package discovery, topological dependency graph ordering, `sharedPaths`/`ignorePaths`, and per-package changelogs.
- 📝 **Rich Changelogs, AI Disclosure & Contributor MVPs** — Keep-a-Changelog Markdown & HTML generation with automatic AI co-author disclosure badges (`🤖`) and first-time contributor / `🏆 Release MVP` recognition.
- 🔐 **Supply-Chain Security by Default** — Keyless Sigstore Cosign v3 (`--bundle`) signatures, CycloneDX & SPDX SBOMs, and SLSA Level 1 provenance attestations.
- 🏢 **Multi-Forge & Enterprise Ready** — First-class support for GitHub.com, GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES `/api/v3` & custom CA), Data Residency (`*.ghe.com`), GitLab CI, Gitea, Forgejo, Bitbucket Cloud, and CircleCI, including automatic PR/MR release comments.
- ✅ **Built-in DX (`doctor` & `commitlint`)** — Pre-flight environment diagnostics (`semrel doctor`), Git-hook commit linting (`semrel commitlint --commit-msg-file`), and IDE autocomplete via published [JSON Schemas](https://www.semrel.io/guide/schemas/).

## Installation

### Docker (Distroless & Alpine)

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/semrels/semrel:latest-alpine
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" -w /workspace ghcr.io/semrels/semrel:latest-alpine release --dry-run
```

### Go Install

```bash
go install github.com/SemRels/semrel/cmd/semrel@latest
semrel --version
```

### Static Binary Download (Linux, macOS, Windows)

```bash
curl -sSL https://github.com/SemRels/semrel/releases/latest/download/semrel_linux_amd64.tar.gz | tar -xz semrel
sudo mv semrel /usr/local/bin/
```

Update `semrel` and manage pinned plugins at any time:

```bash
# Self-update semrel to the latest release
semrel update

# Install official plugins (automatically pinned in .semrel.lock)
semrel plugin install @semrel/condition-github-actions
semrel plugin install @semrel/generator-changelog-md
semrel plugin install @semrel/updater-go
semrel plugin install @semrel/provider-github

# Restore all SHA-256 verified plugins from .semrel.lock in CI
semrel plugin restore
```

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. Create .semrel.yaml (and add .semrel/ and .semrel-analytics.jsonl to .gitignore)
semrel config init

# 2. Verify config, plugins, git state, and environment
semrel doctor

# 3. Validate commit messages since the last tag (or in a Git commit-msg hook)
semrel lint
semrel commitlint --commit-msg-file .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG

# 4. Dry-run release (preview next SemVer version and changelog with zero side effects)
semrel release --dry-run

# 5. Run the full production release pipeline (or monorepo: semrel workspace release)
semrel release --github-output
```

## CLI Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `semrel release` | Run the full semantic release pipeline from commit analysis through tagging, packaging, publishing, and hooks. |
| `semrel workspace release` | Run topological monorepo releases across multiple independent or lockstep packages. |
| `semrel changelog` | Generate unreleased changelog entries without creating a release. |
| `semrel lint` | Validate commits since the last tag against Conventional Commits. |
| `semrel commitlint` | Lint commit messages from the last tag, a git range, `--commit-msg-file`, arguments, or stdin. |
| `semrel doctor` | Run pre-flight checks for `.semrel.yaml`, `.semrel.lock`, plugins, git state, and CI environment. |
| `semrel config init` | Create a new `.semrel.yaml` configuration file and update `.gitignore`. |
| `semrel config show` | Print the resolved configuration. |
| `semrel config validate` | Validate the current configuration file against the core schema. |
| `semrel config set` | Update a top-level or nested configuration key. |
| `semrel migrate` | Upgrade `.semrel.yaml` to the current schema version. |
| `semrel plugin list` | List plugins available in the registry. |
| `semrel plugin search` | Search plugins by name, description, or tag. |
| `semrel plugin install` | Download, verify, and pin a plugin binary in `.semrel.lock`. |
| `semrel plugin update` | Check and apply plugin updates from `.semrel.lock` or a single plugin ref. |
| `semrel plugin restore` | Reinstall SHA-256 pinned plugins from `.semrel.lock` (air-gap friendly). |
| `semrel update` | Check for and install the latest `semrel` release. |

## IDE Support & JSON Schemas

The `.semrel.yaml` config file has a published [JSON Schema](https://registry.semrel.io/schemas/core/v1.json) that enables auto-complete, validation, and hover docs in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, and any LSP-aware editor.

`semrel config init` automatically adds the schema directive. For existing configs, add this line at the top:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://registry.semrel.io/schemas/core/v1.json
```

VS Code users: install the [YAML extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=redhat.vscode-yaml) for full support. See [JSON Schemas documentation](https://www.semrel.io/guide/schemas/) for plugin-level schemas.

## Local Production Demo (semrel + real plugins)

Run an end-to-end local demo that builds `semrel`, builds real plugin binaries from sibling repositories, creates a temporary git repository, and runs a release pipeline using external plugins:

```bash
make local-demo
```

Optional dry-run mode:

```bash
bash scripts/local-demo.sh --dry-run
```

Expected outcome:
- a new demo repository is created in your workspace root
- semrel executes external plugins via `path:` entries
- a new semantic version tag is created (unless `--dry-run` is used)

## Configuration Example (`.semrel.yaml`)

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://registry.semrel.io/schemas/core/v1.json
tagPrefix: v
commit_changelog: false
branches:
  - name: main
  - name: next
    prerelease: beta

plugins:
  - uses: @semrel/condition-github-actions
    phase: condition
  - uses: @semrel/analyzer-conventional
  - uses: @semrel/generator-changelog-md
    phase: pre-tag
    args:
      keep_releases: "10"
      ai_disclosure: "true"
  - uses: @semrel/updater-go
    phase: pre-tag
    args:
      file: internal/version/version.go
  - uses: @semrel/packager-nfpm
    phase: release
  - uses: @semrel/publisher-oci
    phase: release
  - uses: @semrel/provider-github
    phase: release
    args:
      token: "${env.GITHUB_TOKEN}"
      comment_on_prs: "true"
  - uses: @semrel/hook-discord
    phase: release
```

See the [full Configuration Reference](https://www.semrel.io/guide/configuration/) and [docs/config-reference.md](docs/config-reference.md) for all options.

## Architecture

- **Core engine**: Conventional Commits analysis, SemVer calculation, changelog generation, git tag creation
- **Plugin system**: `pkg/plugininstance.Orchestrator` launches standalone plugin binaries in subprocesses
- **Plugin discovery**: `~/.semrel/plugins/semrel-plugin-<name>` first, then `$PATH`

See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for the full design.

## Supply Chain Security

semrel takes supply-chain security seriously:

- **Signed releases**: Artifacts signed with [Sigstore Cosign](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign) (keyless OIDC)
- **SBOM**: CycloneDX 1.4 and SPDX 2.3 Bills of Materials published per release
- **SLSA provenance**: Level 1 build provenance documenting artifact digests
- **DCO**: Developer Certificate of Origin required on all commits
- **REUSE/SPDX**: License compliance enforced in CI on every PR

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for vulnerability reporting and artifact verification instructions.
